children: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has expanded its regulatory framework for vault managers to cover bullion underlying gold and silver exchange-traded funds (ETFs) and bullion derivatives, as the regulator seeks to harmonise standards for the growing bullion market.

The SEBI Board approved amendments to the SEBI (Vault Managers) Regulations, 2021, which were originally introduced to regulate vault managers providing storage and safekeeping services for gold underlying electronic gold receipts (EGRs).
The expanded framework will now cover vaulting services for bullion underlying SEBI-specified bullion-related instruments, including ETFs and derivatives on bullion.

SEBI will replace the EGR-specific provisions with a product-neutral framework covering all specified bullion-related instruments. The regulator will also introduce definitions for "bullion" and "bullion-related instruments".
The net worth requirement for vault managers will be increased to Rs 75 crore from Rs 50 crore.

SEBI will also replace the existing "Gold Standards" terminology with "Bullion Delivery Standards", extending delivery requirements beyond gold underlying EGRs to bullion underlying all specified bullion-related instruments.
The amended framework will strengthen requirements around the storage and safekeeping of bullion, segregation, reconciliation, insurance, security and governance.

Vault managers will have to strengthen their security policies to address risks including theft, burglary, fire, fraud, terrorism and cyberattacks. The risks covered under security policies and procedures for dealing with losses will also be aligned.
The existing requirement for business-wise segregation of activities will be expanded to cover vaulting services provided for all SEBI-specified bullion-related instruments.
Additional requirements will also be introduced for instrument-wise and entity-wise segregation of bullion stored by vault managers.
The regulator will also require vault managers to appoint a compliance officer and specify the officer's broad responsibilities.
SEBI said the amendments are aimed at creating a common regulatory framework as the Indian bullion market evolves with the growth of instruments such as gold and silver ETFs and bullion derivatives.

A consequential circular will set out operational requirements covering storage and safekeeping, quality standards, reconciliation, inspection, audit, insurance, security and infrastructure, risk management and grievance redressal.

The review is intended to create a harmonised and scalable framework for vaulting services across different bullion-related instruments and provide consistent standards for the custody and safekeeping of bullion.

title: SEBI expands vault manager rules to cover gold, silver ETFs and bullion derivatives
